claim: A parallax sky set low covers the view like a ceiling: it is painted from the far wall's top upward, so whatever stands beyond and above it is not drawn. A building made low by lowering the sky in front of it hides everything behind it. (A separate count: in 0 of the 38 campaign maps with open sky are all one-sided walls under the sky drawn to one height.)
evidence: Seen in a run of NBlood by the owner, 2026-11-17: 'when you put parallax sky low it is covering view like a normal ceiling' (projects/blood-city/experiments/church-roofs/README.md:10); the experiment's before/ frames show the tower from the churchyard painting 0 pixels (before-after.png)
tools/mine_skylines.py over the campaign: maps_with_one_wall_height 0 of 38 maps with open sky (43 maps)
use: Raise the floor, never lower the sky: a low mass is a sector whose floor is its top under the common sky. Raise a sky only for the one thing taller than the town.

checked.how: Owner's words found in projects/blood-city/experiments/church-roofs/README.md:10 and hypothesis.json:10 ('when you put parallax sky low it is covering view like a normal ceiling'); README records yard_to_tower painting 0 px of a 17.4-body tower. Ran tools/mine_skylines.py: 43 maps, 38 with open sky, maps_with_one_wall_height 0 - it counts one-sided-wall heights under sky, not lowered skies, so 'no campaign map does it' had no count behind it and is taken out.
